insight: Specs over data modules in `desktop/src` are stub-passable whenever the expected value is read back out of the module under test (`toBe(profile.cliInstall.unix)`), so catalog contents must be asserted as literal strings.

Functions in `desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` that take `&AppHandle` to read `app.path()` cannot be exercised by any spec because `tauri` is declared with `features = []` in Cargo.toml (no `test` feature, so no `mock_app`), so a plan that asserts resolution-order behavior must require the candidate directory list be injectable — otherwise the specs silently degrade into testing an array the test itself built.

The desktop package's `pnpm test` covers only pure logic (`test/rules.test.ts`, `test/catalog.test.ts`) and vite.config has no jsdom/happy-dom environment, so any plan touching `desktop/src/main.ts` or `desktop/index.html` must add a manual verification step — a UI control can be deleted with every gate green.

The Tauri config sets `"csp": null` and main.ts builds several elements via `innerHTML`, so any new `#[tauri::command]` that accepts a free-form string and executes it (shell, path, URL) hands the webview that authority directly — prefer commands that take an identifier and resolve the dangerous value Rust-side.

The test Active Storage service is Disk rooted at `tmp/storage` with no teardown anywhere in `test/test_helper.rb`, so objects survive between suite runs — any spec asserting "uploaded once" or "not present" must generate fresh per-run content or it passes on the first run and fails (or falsely passes) on the next.

This codebase's append-only pattern (`def readonly? = persisted?`, as in Activity) makes `has_many ..., dependent: :destroy` raise ActiveRecord::ReadOnlyRecord when the parent is destroyed — append-only children must cascade via `dependent: :delete_all` or the FK.

A worktree branch created from `origin/main` tracks it; with `push.default=upstream` a bare `git push -u origin <branch>` fast-forwards main itself — set push.default=simple repo-wide and unset the stale upstream before any worker pushes.

Any new table carrying both workspace_id and a parent id (channel_id, agent_session_id, agent_run_id) must get a composite foreign key `column: [<parent>_id, workspace_id], primary_key: [id, workspace_id]` in addition to the plain FK — this is the database-level guard that a child of one workspace cannot reference a parent of another, established in 20260801130001_workspace_id_everywhere.rb and carried by all 5 existing room tables, and adding workspace_id to Workspace::Boundary::ROOMS alone does not provide it.
